questions.q: What's the core difference between usage metrics (Lesson 14) and the audit log (this lesson)?
options: They're the same thing with different names
Usage metrics covers one report's view counts for its owner; the audit log covers every logged action tenant-wide for admins and compliance reviewers
Usage metrics is for admins only; the audit log is for report owners only
The audit log only tracks Power BI Desktop, never the service
questions.explain: Usage metrics answers 'who viewed this report.' The audit log answers the broader question of who did what, to which item, across the whole tenant — visible to admins and compliance reviewers, not just an item's owner.

questions.q: What platform does Power BI's activity auditing actually run through?
options: A separate, Power-BI-only logging tool with no connection to other Microsoft products
Microsoft Purview's unified audit log, the same system used across Microsoft 365
Power BI Desktop's local event viewer
A third-party auditing plugin that must be purchased separately
questions.explain: Power BI activity auditing runs through Microsoft Purview's unified audit log, with Power BI as one of the workloads it covers alongside the rest of Microsoft 365.

questions.q: What information does one row in an audit search result capture?
options: Only the report's title
Date, IP address, user, the type of activity, and the exact item touched
Only whether the action succeeded or failed, with no other detail
The full DAX code of any measure that was edited
questions.explain: Each logged event records when it happened, the IP address it came from, who performed it, what kind of action it was, and the specific item involved.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe audit searches as 'saved jobs' rather than one-off queries?
options: Because results are deleted immediately after viewing them once
Because a reviewer can come back later and check a named search's status and results, which matters for investigations spanning several days
Because Power BI requires a new license for every search
Because audit searches can only be run once per year
questions.explain: Audit searches have a name, a status, and are saved, so a reviewer doesn't have to re-run them from scratch — useful for real investigations that unfold over multiple days.

questions.q: What does drilling into a single audit log event's detail reveal, beyond the summary row?
options: Nothing additional — the summary row already shows everything
A raw, detailed payload — including things like a client app ID and correlation ID — for deeper investigation
The report's full visual layout
A list of every other tenant's audit events
questions.explain: Expanding one event's detail surfaces its full captured payload, down to identifiers like a client app ID and correlation ID — the level of detail a real security or compliance investigation needs.
